Naveen Kumar Kashyap Additional District And Sessions Judge Po Mact, South East District, Saket Courts: New Delhi Mact No.: 389/18 Fir no.: 597/18 Ps :Amar Colony U/s 279, 338 Ipc Cnr No.: Dlse01-001597-2018 Rakesh Kumar S/o Sh. Phool Singh R/o E-65, Harkesh Nagar Okhla Ind. Estate, Phase-I, Okhla Ind. Area, New Delhi-110020. .....Petitioner/claimant Versus Devender S/o Sh. Dharam Singh R/o Village-Bagpur, PO-Bilaspur G B Nagar -201301. ............Driver/Respondent no. 1 Hari Chand S/o Sh. Ramji Lal R/o H.No. 195, Village-Bukharpur, Faridabad, Haryana. ............Owner/Respondent no. 2 Sbi General Insurance Co. texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act. 2. As per the investigation carried out by concerned police official on 29.12.2017, concerned police officials on call received went to the place of accident. There truck bearing no. HR-38W- 1399 and one motorcycle bearing no. HR-07Q-6638 were found in accidental condition but no injured or eye Rakesh Kumar vs Devender on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98667752/ 1 witness was found. It was further came to knowledge of the IO that injured is shifted to Escort Fortis hospital, Delhi. On reaching hospital, injured/claimant Rakesh Kumar was found admitted in hospital. Later on, during investigation, one eye witness Monu Kumar stated that at the time and spot of accident, he saw when he was coming back to his home and waiting at the bus stop at RTP, at about 5.45 pm that a person riding on a one motorcycle was coming from Kalkaji Mandir side and all of a sudden an Eicher canter came from Okhla Mandi side in a rash and negligent manner in high speed and hit such motorcycle. Such motorcycle fell on the road, as a result thereof. Further, driver of offending vehicle truck/vehicle stopped and came out to such injured. Other people also gathered. Further, such complainant also went to that place and driver of the truck was trying to help such injured. But when condition of such motorcyclist/injured started deteriorating, such truck driver tried to run away from the place but he was apprehended by such Monu Kumar and other public MACT No.:389/18 Rakesh v. Devender Page No. 2 of 24 BK and someone called at 100 number and as such driver forcefully run away from such place and such injured/claimant shifted to hospital and later on such complainant made such complaint to the police and recorded his statement. 3. Accordingly, initially FIR u/s 279, 338 IPC was registered. Even the chargesheet u/s 279, 338, IPC filed against the R-1 apart from filing of present DAR. 4. As per record, R-1/driver and R-2/owner filed their reply. In nutshell, it is stated in such reply by R-1&R-2 that no such accident caused by rash and negligent driving of R-1 and present DAR is filed in collusion with police officials by the complainant. It is further claimed that accident if any took place due to sole negligence of injured/claimant of such motorcycle as such motorcyclist hit the canter which was parked properly at the side of the road. As such, it is further claimed that there is no question of paying any compensation to the claimant in the present case. It is further claimed that claimant/injured was not wearing helmet nor holding any driving licence to driver such motorcycle. It is stated that even otherwise such vehicles in question is insured with R-3. 5. Further, reply dated 26.03.2018 filed by insurance company/R-3. In nutshell, it is claimed by R-3 that offending vehicle was insured with such company but same was subject to terms and conditions of such insurance policy. Insurance company also claimed that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of claimant only. 6. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed by learned Predecessor of this Tribunal on 19.12.2018: MACT No.:389/18 Rakesh v. Devender Page No. 3 of 24 BK 1. Rakesh Kumar vs Devender on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98667752/ 2 3. Relief. 7. Claimant/petitioner examined himself as PW-1. Such PW1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents including the discharge summary, MLC, educational certificate, salary slip and medical bills Ex. PW-1/1 to Ex. PW-1/9 and document Mark-A. He was cross-examined at length by learned counsel for insurance company/R-3. 8. Further, one Rakesh Kumar Bhagat, Senior Executive (HR), M/s. Great Value Fuels Pvt. Ltd. was examined as PW-2 to prove the income related documents from employer. He proved on record attested copy of appointment letter as Ex. PW-2/B, Salary slip for the month of September to December, 2017 and December, 2019, Ex. PW-2/C(Colly). Further, leave certificate is proved as Ex. PW-2/D. This witness was also cross-examined by learned counsel for R-3/insurance company. 9. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 10. No witness was examined by respondent side. 14. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal. 19. Accordingly, the issue No.1 is decided accordingly, in favour of the petitioner. Furthermore, even during cross-examination of PW-1/injured, a suggestion was put that such injured was wearing helmet but same is denied.
texts.arguments: In Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 15. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 21. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered Rakesh Kumar vs Devender on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98667752/ 4 as a result of such injury. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). 22.5. Assessment of non-pecuniary damages--Items (iv), (v) and (vi)--involves determination of l u m p s u m a m o u n t s w i t h r e f e r e n c e t o c i r c u m s t a n c e s s u c h a s a g e , n a t u r e o f injury/deprivation/disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant. 22.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 22.7. 36. On the other hand, it is argued by Ld. Counsel for insurance company that there is no functional disability of 45 % MACT No.:389/18 Rakesh v. Devender Page No. 12 of 24 BK in the present case. It is further argued that there is no functional disability in the present case at all which is also clear from cross- examination of such witness. He further deposed that since the time of joining, such claimant/injured is working properly and he has rejoined on the updated/current salary, alongwith previous admissible perks and incentives. 38. Such situation is also dealt in such landmark case of Rajkumar (supra), where it is noted, that in a particular case like in present case, there may be physical/psychological disability but still no functional disability. It may be noted that in the judgment of Ram Charan & Ors. Vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., MAC Appeal no. 433/2013, decided on 18.10.2022 it was noted regarding rate of interest: "25 to evaluate the submission made by counsel for the applicants, it is imperative to examine the guiding principles for the grant of interest. In Abati Bezbaruah Vs. Geological Survey of India, (2003) 3 SCC 148, the following was held while interpreting section 171 of the MV Act, 1988:- Three decisions were cited before us by Mr. A. P. Mohanty, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Appellant, in support of his contentions. The rate of interest must be just and reasonable depending upon the facts and circumstances of each case and taking all relevant factors including inflation, change of economy, policy being adopted by Reserve Bank of India from time to time, how long the case is pending, permanent injuries suffered by MACT No.:389/18 Rakesh v. Devender Page No. 16 of 24 BK the victim, enormity of suffering, loss of future income, loss of enjoyment of life etc. into consideration. Therefore, in my opinion, there cannot be any hard and fast rule in awarding interest and the award of interest is solely on the discretion of the Tribunal of the High Court Rakesh Kumar vs Devender on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98667752/ 10 as indicated above." 42. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 9% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. 43. The total compensation payable to the claimant would be Rs.3,57,840/- with simple interest at the rate of 9% p.a. from the MACT No.:389/18 Rakesh v. Devender Page No. 17 of 24 BK date of filing of DAR till its actual realization. LIABILITY:- 44. 45. The award amount shall be deposited with State Bank of India, Saket Court Branch, New Delhi by way of RTGS/NEFT/IMPS in account of MACT FUND PARKING, A/c No. 35195787436, IFS Code SBIN0014244 and MICR code 110002342 under intimation to the Nazir along with calculation of interest and to the Counsel for the petitioner. 46. This court is in receipt of the orders dated 07.12.2018 passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in FAO no. 842/2003 titled as Rajesh Tyagi & Ors. Vs. Jaibir Singh & Ors whereby the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has formulated MACAD(Motor Accident Claims Annuity Deposit Scheme) which has been made effective from 01.01.2019. The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD formulated by the Hon'ble High Court MACT No.:389/18 Rakesh v. Devender Page No. 18 of 24 BK of Delhi. Apportionment:- 47. 48. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: Rakesh Kumar vs Devender on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98667752/ 11 "...... In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". In the case of illiterate claimants, the Tribunal is allowed to consider the request for lumpsum payment for effecting purchase of any movable property such as agricultural implements, rickshaws etc. to earn a living. In the case of semi-illiterate claimants, the Tribunal should ordinarily invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. The guidelines were not MACT No.:389/18 Rakesh v. Devender Page No. 20 of 24 BK to be understood to mean that the Tribunals were to take a rigid stand while considering an application seeking release of the money. However, it is seen that even in cases when there is no possibility or chance of the feed being frittered away by the beneficiary owing to ignorance, illiteracy or susceptibility to exploitation, investment of the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit is directed by the Rakesh Kumar vs Devender on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98667752/ 12 Tribunals as a matter of course and in a routine manner, ignoring the object and the spirit of the guidelines issued by this Court and the genuine requirements of the claimants.
